selection_note: Upstream upgrade batch 26: five most recently reviewed distinct available included S1=A / S2=C canonical Index assessments at 85ae995f, excluding identities from all 25 integrated batch manifests and source-to-fork registry. Reviewed-at descending order. S2 predictions, expected benefit and explicit null/falsifiers publicly committed as 8229aad before any fresh original repository code/issues/policy inspection. Selection is five testable questions, not five admitted fixes.

candidates.finding: Check whether a supported cancelled or failed dispatch can retain the shared one-token mutation lock and indefinitely prevent a later agent task from accessing DATA_ROOT.
candidates.screening_result: Current original main@7d576a3 AGPL-3.0. The one-token chain is acquired before runner work, with deferred release after accounting and a later-registered recover defer. Existing source-native first-party tests exercise panic in model and script runner; ordinary failure/cancel does not prove a stranded token. A failure inside deferred accounting could bypass its trailing release, but no reachable matched native reproducer or maintainer need has been established. Source inspection only; no tests or derivative patch run.
candidates.blocker: No supported first-party accounting/monitor panic or cancellation path reproduces a leaked dispatch token; existing model/script panic regression recovery passes historically. A theoretical secondary defer panic is not an admitted product defect.

candidates.finding: Check whether concurrent run_next invocations can separately select and then claim same-project work outside one SQLite transaction, despite project lock and dependency readiness.
candidates.screening_result: Current original main@4194010 MIT. Kernel.run_next calls run and _start, which validates fresh task version/status, capacity, inserts attempt, acquires project lock and sets STARTING within one Store.tx. Store.tx begins BEGIN IMMEDIATE and project_locks has unique project_id primary key; concurrent conflicting admission becomes Busy(project_locked) or Busy(changed). The hypothesized separate-check/claim race is already closed by first-party code. Static source check only; no new native test, patch, issue or PR.

candidates.finding: Check whether a review-round acceptance overlapping a still-outstanding delegated child or remediation step can advance parent readiness from an obsolete state snapshot.
candidates.screening_result: Current original default main and contributor dev both @66a24ea Apache-2.0. Review reply checks task and meeting states, and delegation uses an in-flight set and queued follow-up. Neither constitutes a proven atomic interleaving of all parent/child transitions, but no observed native stale parent completion was produced. PR #91 modifies directive integration/parallel department planning (55 files) on dev and overlaps the proposed mechanism; CONTRIBUTING requires external contributions to target dev with CI/review. No separate native test, patch, external fork write or PR.
candidates.blocker: No isolated supported stale parent-readiness counterexample or matched native interleaving; concurrently open 55-file PR #91 changes directive integration and parallel planning, and contributor PRs must target dev.

candidates.finding: Check whether the existing bilateral worker slot reservation can be bypassed at a supported capacity boundary while the opposite workload class has ready cards.
candidates.screening_result: Current original main@92c49bf Apache-2.0 drifted from assessed c20297f. First-party class_cap explicitly returns cap-1 for max_in_progress >=2, else no reservation for cap 1. ReservedSlot counts per class and holds_back denies spawn when a class already holds its cap. On state-read failures the code deliberately fails open to preserve dispatch, which is a declared compatibility policy, not an observed concurrency defect. No supported bypass identified. CONTRIBUTING requires Google CLA personal assent; no external action or native test performed.

candidates.finding: Check whether overlap-warning cooldown can suppress new feedback after the shared-context TTL expires but before an affected issue worker consumes that warning.
candidates.screening_result: Current original main@e7c160f MIT. Supervisor CONFLICT_DEDUP_WINDOW_MS=120000 (2 min) while ContextEntryDraft TTL=1800000 (30 min); repeated conflict after dedup writes project-scoped shared context unconditionally, even if per-worker steer cooldown stops a direct steer event. The proposed expiration-before-dedup loss is therefore contradicted by current first-party code, and existing supervisor tests cover conflict reporting and cooldown separately. No new tests or source edits performed.
